clue.text: Share second footballer

parts.note: a half is a share, one of two equal parts
to second someone is to back or support them

explanation.surface: Someone splits the takings with a second-string player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' is the verb meaning support, as when a speaker seconds a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfback is a player positioned between the forwards and the backs in football or rugby.

clue.text: Billyboy

annotationWithheld.why: Billyboy: OCR of what is likely 'Bully boy', a double definition (hector = bully; Hector a boy's name), but the repair could not be filed for this one-word clue

clue.text: Fat about to turn up in food store

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: in a down clue to turn up means the word for about is read from bottom to top

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Fat is about to appear in the pantry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reverses RE to ER; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool room or cupboard where food is kept.

clue.text: Song and dance over notice

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the dance above the notice

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A song and dance made over a public notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song and dance' is a fixed phrase for a fuss; split it, 'Song' defines and 'dance' is BALL, placed 'over' AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative song or poem.

clue.text: Scores like to go through with marriage knot to be tied

annotationWithheld.why: Scores like to go through with marriage knot to be tied: HITCH is marriage and the definition is 'knot to be tied', but no reading of 'Scores like to go through' gives CLOVE; likely a garbled OCR word.

clue.text: Wind up phone

explanation.surface: Someone cranks the handle of an old telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: BLOWER is British slang for the telephone; 'Wind up' reads as cranking a handle but is the sense of something that drives air upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A blower is a machine that drives a current of air up a flue; 'the blower' is British slang for the telephone.

clue.text: I want to consider request for vision

explanation.surface: Someone asks for time to think and for a look.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase both buys thinking time and asks to be shown something.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said when pausing to think, and also when asking to be shown something.

clue.text: Headgear from the west ought to suit so why the fuss?

parts.note: a hat is headgear
ought is an old spelling of aught or nought, zero, the letter O
to fit is to suit

explanation.surface: A western hat ought to fit, so what is all the fuss about?
explanation.walkthrough: 'ought' is the old form of nought, giving O; 'from the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dismissive retort meaning it does not matter.

clue.text: Do harps maybe before end of day inspired music?

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the two words could be arranged another way
end of picks the final letter of day

explanation.surface: Might harps, played at dusk, stir a composer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges DO HARPS into RHAPSOD; 'end of' takes the Y of 'day'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsody is an effusive, freely structured musical composition.

clue.text: Motor suffering on bells

parts.note: motor is an everyday British word for a car
suffering means ill, unwell

explanation.surface: A broken-down car is making a racket of bells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' looks like an anagram signal working on 'Motor', but it is just ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A carillon is a set of tuned bells played from a keyboard, usually in a tower.

clue.text: Way artist thanks a lot of layers

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
TA is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: An artist on the street thanks a passer-by for a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: RA (Royal Academician) and TA (British for 'thanks') are crossword staples.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata is the plural of stratum, so it names many layers of rock or society.

clue.text: Chose to have period in included as worked

indicators.note: included tells us one piece goes within the other, the period sitting inside the word for chose

parts.note: to opt is to choose, so chose gives opted
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone decided to add a full stop where it fit the work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' puts ERA inside OPTED; the newspaper text split the word into 'in eluded'.
explanation.definitionFit: Operated and worked are synonyms for a machine or person functioning.

clue.text: Chap with plenty of ancient slaves

parts.note: he refers to a chap, a man
lots means plenty

explanation.surface: A man with a great many slaves of old.
explanation.definitionFit: Helots were the serf class of ancient Sparta, bound to the land.

clue.text: Trickiest prospect in protective clothing

explanation.surface: The most tricky outlook in body armour.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge a strong suit is the one promising the most tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the strong suit offers the best chance of tricks; a strong suit could also be sturdy protective garb.

clue.text: Wren for instance as a source of information

explanation.surface: A wren is the informant who passes on news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little bird told me' is the idiom for an unnamed informant.
explanation.definitionFit: A wren is a tiny songbird; the phrase also names the unnamed tipster in 'a little bird told me'.

clue.text: Nail playwright to timetable

parts.note: a brad is a thin flat nail
George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright

explanation.surface: Fixing a dramatist to the train schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Bradshaw was the famous British railway timetable guide.
explanation.definitionFit: Bradshaw's guide was the standard railway schedule in Victorian Britain.

clue.text: I do after a time become a worshipper

parts.note: taken as written
later means after a time

explanation.surface: Someone vows to take up worship in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I do' evokes the marriage vow; 'become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols or excessively adores something.

clue.text: Bet on run with animal

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the bet above the run

parts.note: an ante is a stake, a bet
to lope is to run with long strides

explanation.surface: A gambler puts money on a race with a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An antelope is a fleet, horned grazing mammal of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Whip getting in harvest in part of Yorkshire

parts.note: Yorkshire was historically divided into three Ridings
a crop is a harvest

explanation.surface: A farmer cracks a whip while bringing in the harvest somewhere in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ridings were the three historic divisions of Yorkshire, an English county; 'in' is only a link here, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A riding crop is a short whip used by horse riders.

clue.text: A close form of comfort

indicators.note: form of says the letters are made into a new shape

explanation.surface: A close embrace is a kind of consolation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges A CLOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is consolation in distress.

clue.text: Severely criticise a parent in hat

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
ma is mother, a parent

explanation.surface: Lambasting a mother in her headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a lightweight straw hat.

clue.text: Article, after that eastern goddess

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
then means after that

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece followed by an Eastern deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene is the Greek goddess of wisdom, also spelt Athena.

clue.text: Sweet pair about fifty, a hundred once

indicators.note: about says the word for pair goes round the other letters

parts.note: a duet is a pair of performers
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, as the Romans once wrote it

explanation.surface: A sweet couple around fifty used to be worth a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L and C, Roman numerals, inside DUET.
explanation.definitionFit: Dulcet describes something sweet and soothing, mostly sounds.

clue.text: Not knowing if soldier came back without any bluster

indicators.note: came back tells us the word for soldier is read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
no means without any, as in no money
a rant is loud bluster

explanation.surface: Unaware whether the soldier returned without any shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came back' turns GI into IG; 'if' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant means lacking knowledge or awareness.

clue.text: Poker in fire of supercharged car

explanation.surface: A poker left in the fire becomes a souped-up car.
explanation.walkthrough: A poker left in the fire is literally a hot rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot rod is a car modified for speed; a poker heated in the fire is a hot metal rod.

clue.text: Manage to stone vagabond

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
agate is a semi-precious stone

explanation.surface: Someone manages to stone a tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A runagate is an archaic word for a wanderer or fugitive.

clue.text: Tip off soldiers inside maze

indicators.note: inside places the soldiers within the phrase for tip off

parts.note: to tip someone off is to warn them
RE is the Royal Engineers, soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are alerted inside a labyrinth.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A warren is a maze of tunnels or narrow passages.

clue.text: Guide has time to find cheap part of ship

parts.note: to steer is to guide
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A guide takes the time to find the budget section of a liner.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage is the lowest-priced passenger accommodation on a ship.
